author: rdc-rfc1-author-b (Claude Haiku 5.5)
workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
rationale: trained_q has two asynchronous controls that force opposite values, and the functional link_drop_ni clear has priority over the reset preset. Its value during and after overlapping assertion depends on priority and release order.

author_reading.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
author_reading.rationale: The functional asynchronous clear is checked before reset, so when link_drop_ni is low while rst_ni asserts, trained_q is cleared instead of taking its reset-to-one value.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: rst_ni both sets trained_q (negedge event, then the synchronous branch !rst_ni sets 1) and is read as data. Reset therefore forces the training flag to 1, not 0, while link_drop_ni clears it. The stored state during reset does not reflect a reset value.
labels.suspected_flaw: The comment says the block tracks whether link training has completed, but the reset branch sets trained_q to 1. That contradicts a normal reset value of 0.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: The asynchronous controls force opposite values. Releasing link_drop_ni when rst_ni remains asserted leaves trained_q clear until a clock edge despite the remaining asynchronous set request.
labels.suspected_flaw: The reset branch also sets trained before any reported training completion.

settlement.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical, class and RDC-026. RDC-019 (A) does not apply: rst_ni is used only as an asynchronous control. RDC-002, RDC-003 and RDC-011 are incidental. Sites follow B.
